mutations.name: gemini guard re-gated on having started emitting — a stream that died with zero content falls through to finishReason:STOP again. The replacement reconstructs the old `this.started` faithfully (it was set by emitTextDelta on non-empty text and by bufferToolCall) rather than referencing the deleted field, because an undefined field would disable the guard ENTIRELY and inject a different, larger defect than the one being re-introduced

gemini guard over-reaches: ANY frameless stream errors, so a legitimately empty completion that terminated properly (bare [DONE]) becomes an UNAVAILABLE error — the half-wrong fix that turns working requests into failures
anthropic guard re-gated on messageStarted — a stream that died before any parseable chunk reports stop_reason:end_turn with zero error events again
anthropic guard over-reaches: a properly terminated stream that never started a message (bare [DONE]) errors instead of closing cleanly — the same half-wrong fix on the other frontend

the lazy message_start on the clean-close path stops firing, so a legitimately empty completion emits message_delta + message_stop with no preceding message_start — the exact sequence Claude Code reports as "Content block not found"

the same started-gate defect injected into responses.js, the frontend that already got this right. It is the reference the other two were aligned to, so the three-way parity assertion must fail when the reference itself regresses — otherwise that assertion is only checking the two handlers this change touched
